subject: Day 27: narrate a diaper change
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 27 closes out week 4. The high-leverage move today is turning ordinary caregiving into dense language and music exposure, since the serve-and-return cadence is what compounds.

Action items
- Narrate the next diaper change step by step in warm, sing-song speech; routine tasks are some of the densest language exposure he gets, and Romeo et al. tied conversational turns to later language outcomes. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Confirm the 1-month well visit is on the books for the day 28-35 window if you have not locked it in yet. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- Pre-write Anoushka's questions for the 6-week postpartum OB visit now: pelvic floor symptoms, mood, contraception, and the timeline for returning to exercise.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Increasing evening fussiness and a blocked tear duct that weeps from one eye without redness are both common and need no action.
- [monitor] Track any crying that trends toward 3-plus hours a day across multiple days; this is the run-up to the week-6 crying peak, and coping strategies matter more than a colic label.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with poor weight gain warrants a same-day call to rule out pyloric stenosis.
- [call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F or higher, blue lips while crying, or any seizure-like activity is an emergency under 90 days; call the pediatrician or 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Narrate the diaper change in full sentences with a sing-song lilt; describing each step turns a daily chore into rich language input. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Add a football-hold tummy-time variant, draping him belly-down along your forearm, to vary the position as you build toward 20-30 minutes a day. AAP tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Sing live during the change rather than playing a recording; the serve-and-return cadence drives the benefit, not the polish of the song. Music and infant development: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; bring the feeding and output log
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1
- Day 57-72: post-2-month-vaccine window; expect 24-48h of fussiness and low-grade fever

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
